DharmaNexus identifies 96 internal text-reuse matches between this apadāna and six other Pali texts, demonstrating substantial verbatim reuse within the Pali commentarial corpus [DharmaNexus]. In particular, virtually the entire apadāna (§0.3–28.4) is embedded within the second part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (34 matches, 6,682 shared characters), along with additional matches in the first volume of the same commentary (41 matches, 1,984 characters) [DharmaNexus]. Formulaic and thematic verse segments are also shared with several other apadāna texts, including the *Ñāṇathavikattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 486), the *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8), the *Ekachattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 414), and the *Mahāmoggallānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 4) [DharmaNexus].

Beyond Pali, automated text alignment via DharmaNexus suggests low-scoring text reuse with Tibetan texts, including the *Samādhirājasūtra* (D0127) and the *Bodhisattvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155) [DharmaNexus]. These cross-language alignments are machine-generated rather than established parallels [DharmaNexus].
